remaining: Every field offset, constant, branch condition, and the full nested nesting shape (phase==0 -> masked=control&0x88; masked==8 -> serial_error=(u8)(control&4); serial_error==0 && send_index==-1 -> IME/IE/SIOCNT-hi/IF/TM3CNT reconfiguration + mode=masked; phase=1; sequence++) is confirmed instruction-by-instruction against games/gs1/asm/08005fcc.s and matches m2c's independent reading of the same reference bytes. The sole residual defect is register-role assignment: the compiler consistently binds the four function-lifetime locals (state, siocnt, control, masked) to {r4,r7,r6,r5} in that declaration order, while the reference binds the identical four roles to {r7,r6,r5,r4} -- a full cyclic rotation of the same register set, not a semantic difference. Ten independent rephrasings were tried and scored with candidate-show (assignment order of state/siocnt swapped; control read via the siocnt pointer vs. directly through the REG_SIOCNT macro; siocnt as a persistent volatile u32* vs. eliminated in favor of a raw literal cast at each use; masked promoted to function scope vs. left block-scoped; the IME=0 store written as a literal vs. reusing the already-zero serial_error register; the IE read-modify-write collapsed into one compound expression vs. kept as three statements with an explicit ie temporary) and every variant reproduced the exact same {r4,r7,r6,r5} binding or made the match strictly worse (removing the ie temporary also broke the movs-immediate encoding of REG_IME=1 into a spurious literal-pool load and disturbed the phase=1 fallthrough into an extra branch). No PERM_GENERAL/PERM_INT register forcing, asm(), or register-hint escape was used, per the hard constraint against hand-tuning register assignment.
